A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LUVE framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including the new Appendix I in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation comparisons, ablations, reconstruction and efficiency experiments, and a human preference study in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds spectral diagnostics, an attention-map comparison, and qualitative generation examples.

M1.justification: The three-stage LMG/VLU/HCR pipeline, latent upsampler, reconstruction losses, and frequency-filtered LoRA experts remain unchanged in Sections 3.1-3.4 and Appendix C. The added diagnostics analyze the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions use UltraVideo training data, VBench evaluation prompts, and UltraHR-eval4k references for FIDpatch. Appendix I adds examples within the existing 2K/4K video-generation task, without establishing a new dataset, domain, or distinct testing condition.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same Wan2.1, UltraWan, and CineScale entries and the same VSR comparators: RealBasicVSR, VEnhancer, STAR, and FlashVSR. Human-study comparator membership also remains unchanged. The new attention visualization is a component ablation.

E3.justification: v2 introduces diagnostic protocols: PSD measurements of Wan2.1-1.3B latents at native resolution and timesteps 900, 600, 300, and 0 (Figure 6), plus subject-token attention visualization with and without LFE (Figure 12). Existing benchmark, training, and human-study settings are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses examine frequency evolution during denoising (Figure 6) and LFE's effect on attention localization (Figure 12). Appendix I also adds qualitative comparisons against the base model. These supplement the retained upsampling, expert, data-curation, skipped-step, and reconstruction ablations.

E5.justification: The human-study confidence intervals at 95% and 97.5% were already reported in v1's Appendix E and Table 13 and remain unchanged. v2 introduces no additional seed information, repeated-run reporting, or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All existing table values are retained; for example, LUVE's 2K/4K FIDpatch scores remain 41.03/39.87 in Table 2. New findings show low-frequency signals emerging first during denoising and more concentrated attention with LFE. Figures 14-16 add qualitative outputs, without establishing improved benchmark performance over v1.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(5), the losses, and the mathematical descriptions of the upsampler and experts are unchanged. The spectral and attention additions are empirical analyses, without new formal definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, novelty discussion, and conclusion retain the same claims about latent cascading, arbitrary-resolution upsampling, dual-frequency experts, and improved semantic/detail fidelity. The new Impact Statement largely restates this positioning.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 adds the explanation that LFE's semantic constraints concentrate otherwise scattered subject-token attention and preserve global coherence. Section 3.4 connects the new PSD observations to expert specialization. The computational-efficiency limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: The existing architecture specifications, hyperparameters, hardware, inference schedules, data processing, and MLLM evaluation prompts remain unchanged, including Appendices B-F and H. The project link is also unchanged. The added diagnostics supply evaluation settings but no new implementation or access instructions.

R1.justification: Appendix G prunes and redistributes citations, and the bibliography removes works including AddSR, DragFlow, and several Peng et al. papers. The main three-part related-work discussion and LUVE's central positioning remain intact; changed citation-year suffixes do not represent new works.

P1.justification: v2 adds short diagnostic explanations, Appendix I, a conflict-of-interest disclosure, acknowledgments, and an Impact Statement. Publication and author-contribution text are updated. Most prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The visual presentation expands substantially through a four-panel PSD plot, paired attention heatmaps, and three full-page qualitative montages (Figures 6, 12, and 14-16). Existing figures and tables are redistributed and renumbered where needed, while their original content is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly strengthens the frequency-based rationale with direct spectral evidence and an attention-map case study, while additional examples make output quality easier to inspect. The gain is limited: attention evidence concerns a specific prompt, diagnostic implementation details remain sparse, and benchmark results and statistical validation are unchanged.
